description: Checks a website migration, relaunch, redesign, domain or CMS move: compares the old site (Site A) with the new one (Site B) page by page for missing pages, changed content and visual regressions. Free up to 40 pages a day per client address, no key needed. It is priced per page compared. sourceUrl and targetUrl let discovery pick the pages (maxPages caps them), or urls names the pairs; then wait_for_comparison until it ends and get_report with failedOnly: true. dryRun: true answers the page count and price (0.02 USD a page, 0.01 beyond 1000) without charging, and freeCovers without a key; a job above the remaining free allowance is refused with a payment challenge with nextSteps for your human. maxPriceUsd refuses a dearer job before any challenge, never a free job. Answers with jobId, jobToken, status, pagesCharged and, on a free run, sample and allowanceRemaining.

callbackUrl.description: Optional https URL (port 443) that receives one JSON POST when the job ends (jobId, status, summary, links; never the jobToken), a nudge to read the job. Public hosts only, no redirects followed, retried twice; delivery never affects the job.

checkMode.description: What each page is checked on: full (existence, content and visual, the default), text-only (existence and content, no screenshots) or existence-only (only that every page exists and answers, as for a site translated into another language; content and visual are reported as skipped with reason not-requested).

dryRun.description: Quote only: runs every check and the pricing, then answers the page count and exact amount. Nothing is charged, the free allowance is not used and no job starts; the same body without dryRun is priced from the retained result.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional opaque string a retry repeats: under a prepaid balance the same value within 24 hours is not charged again and answers DUPLICATE_REQUEST with the jobId of the first call.

maxPages.description: Optional ceiling on the pages compared and charged for. The job is priced on the pages it compares: the urls list, or the pages discovery finds, at most this many. There is no page limit.

maxPriceUsd.description: Optional spend cap in USD. A job priced above it is refused before any challenge, so an auto-paying client is never asked for more.

sourceAuth.description: HTTP basic auth for Site A.

password.description: Password typed into the sign-in form.

username.description: Username typed into the sign-in form.

sourceLogin.description: Sign-in form login for Site A, or "none" to compare it as is. A site behind a sign-in form is refused unpaid without either. Needs a browser, not text-only.

sourceUrl.description: Site A, the reference site (full URL). Required unless urls is given.

targetAuth.description: HTTP basic auth for Site B.

password.description: Password typed into the sign-in form.

username.description: Username typed into the sign-in form.

targetLogin.description: Sign-in form login for Site B, or "none" to compare it as is. A site behind a sign-in form is refused unpaid without either. Needs a browser, not text-only.

targetUrl.description: Site B, the migrated site. Omit to capture screenshots of Site A only.

threshold.description: Visual diff tolerance as a fraction from 0 (exact) to 1: 0.05 means 5%. The web app takes a percentage; the API does not.

urls.description: Explicit page pairs to compare (at most 50000); skips discovery and is priced per pair. One pair is a single-page comparison and needs no sourceUrl.

target.description: The same page's URL on Site B.

visual.description: Capture rules applied to both sides.

freeze.description: Switches that stop motion before the screenshot.

animations.description: Stop CSS animations and transitions before the screenshot.

clock.description: Pause timers and the clock after load; a page that needs a timer to render may stay empty.

clockSeconds.description: With clock: seconds the clock runs after load before it stops (1 to 600, default 60).

masks.description: CSS selectors of elements hidden on both sites before the screenshot (at most 50, each up to 200 characters). The layout keeps its place.
